title: DOM events, bubbling, capturing, and delegation
hook: A click on a button travels through the DOM in three phases — capture down, target, bubble up. Event delegation attaches one listener on a parent and handles children dynamically, which is how large lists stay fast.

blocks.text: The **DOM event model** dispatches **Event** objects through ancestors. **Capture phase** runs root→target; **target phase** at the element; **bubble phase** target→root. **addEventListener(type, handler, { capture: true })** listens during capture. **stopPropagation** halts further travel; **preventDefault** blocks default browser action (not propagation). **Event delegation** listens on a stable ancestor and uses **event.target** to identify which child was clicked.

entries.plainDefinition: Event propagates from target up through ancestors after target handlers run.
entries.example: Click on <li> bubbles to <ul> then document.

entries.plainDefinition: Propagation from window down to target before bubble phase.
Single listener on parent handles events from many dynamic children.
Deepest element that triggered the event — may differ from currentTarget (listener owner).
entries.example: List item click: target is button, currentTarget is ul.

blocks.text: Tables with 10,000 rows cannot attach 10,000 listeners — delegation plus one handler scales. React's synthetic event system historically delegated to document (legacy) — understanding native phases explains stopPropagation bugs. Shadow DOM retargets events — senior web question. C# UI (WPF/Blazor) routes events differently; browser capture/bubble is unique to DOM.

blocks.title: Interview trap: stopPropagation vs preventDefault
blocks.body: preventDefault stops form submit or link navigation — does not stop bubbling. stopPropagation stops other listeners on ancestors — does not cancel default action unless default is cancelable.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Confusing target with currentTarget. stopPropagation breaking unrelated delegated handlers. Forgetting closest() null check. Attaching duplicate listeners on every render without removing old ones.

blocks.text: Passive event listeners `{ passive: true }` for touch/wheel — browser can scroll without waiting for JS. **pointer-events** and hit testing for overlays. For SPAs, use delegation at stable root; in React 17+ events attach to root container — know your framework's delegation model. Measure listener count in DevTools Performance → Event Listeners.

rows: Events that do not bubble (focus, blur)

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot draw capture vs bubble order. Saying preventDefault stops propagation. Not knowing which events do not bubble (focus, blur, scroll on elements).

interviewTakeaways: DOM events: capture down, target, bubble up — default listeners are bubble phase.
Delegation: one parent listener + event.target.closest selector.
60s: Three phases. Delegate on stable ancestor for dynamic lists. target vs currentTarget. focus/blur do not bubble — use focusin/focusout.
Follow-up: how would you handle 10k row table clicks without 10k listeners?
commonPitfalls: Binding new listeners on every re-render without cleanup.
Using stopPropagation when preventDefault was needed for form submit.
Strong answer: three phases diagram, delegation with closest, non-bubbling events list.

jsTsCorrelations.note: HTMLElementEventMap gives typed event.currentTarget in strict handlers — still same capture/bubble runtime.
Node EventEmitter has no capture/bubble — DOM delegation is a tree-propagation feature unique to browsers.
